Subject: Dataflow variant scoping and DPF requirements — initial package

Hi Priya / OrchidMed team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I attached a compact evidence package that maps the key DPF topics against the deployment variants we've discussed (Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Redwood Private on-prem). The attached workbook (redwood_dataflow_variant_matrix.xlsx) summarizes where data enters/exits Redwood-controlled infrastructure, where customer-controlled keys are required, and typical retention/traceability expectations.

To keep our follow-up targeted, can you confirm the two variants you want us to scope in detail:
- Variant A: Hosted API with EU/US region routing + prefix/KV caching enabled
- Variant B: Private deployment (customer VPC) with optional on-prem model serving and KMS integration

Specific items we want to validate for your legal/security reviewers so our DPA annex can be precise:
- Subprocessor list you require for the data export mapping (any local cloud providers besides AWS/GCP?)
- Whether OrchidMed requires HSM-backed key escrow or standard KMS key wrap
- Acceptable audit log retention window (we typically provide 90/180/365 day tiers)
- Any required redaction/PII minimization on model inputs before persistence in logs or object stores

Attachments included: dpf-evidence-summary.pdf (narrative + control references), redwood_dataflow_variant_matrix.xlsx (variant-by-variant mapping), and a link to a mutual action plan template.

I'll leave Kimberly (privacy engineering) and Laura (legal ops) in copy — they'll provide the technical and annex wording. If useful, we can schedule a short tech-to-tech call to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,

Markus,

Thanks for the concise package. A few clarifying Qs from our side (legal + infra):

1) For Variant A (Hosted API) — our regulator wants concrete statements about when model KV cache fragments are persisted and whether those fragments may cross borders. Can you confirm if the KV cache shard placement follows request region strictly, or if Redwood may route warm cached segments from other regions for cost reasons?

2) For Variant B (Private) — we need to ensure the customer-managed VPC option can be configured such that no inference request logs or artifacts write to Redwood-managed object storage. Is that supported out of the box, or does it require a hybrid (some infra still in Redwood control)?

3) KMS/HSM: We have an enterprise HSM provider and want to require HSM-based key wrapping for model weights at rest (not just KMS). Can you list the specific HSM integrations and whether the DPA annex supports a clause for HSM-only key handling?

4) Subprocessors: we run a local analytics provider in APAC (DataSense Asia). If we opt for Variant A with geo-routing to APAC, will DataSense be included as a subprocessor, or would it only be used if we explicitly route analytics?

5) Audit logs: our baseline expectation is 1 year retention with tamper-evident signing. Can you confirm Redwood supports that retention tier and provides WORM or signed-log evidence?

We're hoping Kimberly can answer the technical points and Laura can advise on annex-level language. If you prefer a short 30-min call next week, Anita (copied) can coordinate.

Best,

Priya
Chief Privacy Officer, OrchidMed Research
priya.sethi@orchidmed.com

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below; I've also attached a short evidence PDF that maps these items to controls and suggested DPA annex language.

1) KV cache placement (Hosted API):
- Default behavior: KV cache shards are scoped to the serving cluster in the request region. We do not replicate warm cache shards cross-region as a cost optimization.
- Exceptions: in rare failover events we may route traffic to a warm standby in a secondary region; these events are documented in our routing policy and covered by the fallback section of the DPA annex. If OrchidMed requires an explicit prohibition on cross-border cache warming, we can add that clause to the annex and enable region-strict routing for your tenant.

2) Private deployment object store isolation:
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports a configuration where all inference artifacts (temporary cache, logs, and model weights) are written to customer-managed storage endpoints only (S3-compatible or on-prem object store). No artifacts are written to Redwood-managed buckets when that mode is enabled.
- For hybrid Dedicated deployments, some control plane telemetry remains in Redwood's control (SLO/uptime metrics) but payload logs can be redacted or sent to customer endpoints based on the deploy profile.

3) HSM integrations:
- We support customer-managed KMS integrations and partner HSMs via the KMIP standard and select cloud HSM providers (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys, and Thales Luna integrations).
- Annex language: we can add an HSM-only control clause and conditional subprocessor disclosure for key escrow operations. Note that live model execution requires keys to be available to the serving hosts; in Private mode these keys never leave the customer HSM boundary.

4) Subprocessors and APAC analytics:
- DataSense Asia: Redwood will only list a subprocessor if we route customer data to them or they process telemetry on Redwood's behalf. If OrchidMed explicitly configures analytics forwarding to DataSense, we will include them in the subprocessor list and provide the required DPA exhibits. If you choose Hosted API without analytics forwarding, DataSense will not be engaged.

5) Audit logs and tamper evidence:
- Retention: we support configurable retention tiers including 365 days.
- Tamper-evidence: we provide signed log bundles (SHA256 + signing certificate) on request and can offer an append-only export (WORM) delivered to a customer-controlled endpoint. For high-assurance requirements we recommend Private deployment + dedicated log export to the customer's SIEM.

Attachments I added: dpf-evidence-summary.pdf (answers mapped to controls), redwood_dataflow_variant_matrix.xlsx (updated variant notes). I also included suggested DPA annex snippets for each item you highlighted.

Next steps proposal:
- Please confirm whether OrchidMed wants Appendix A (Hosted strict-region routing) enabled, or to proceed with Private deployment scoping.
- If Private, we will send a short checklist for the infra team to complete (network CIDRs, KMS/HSM endpoint info, object-store credentials for export).

Happy to jump on a call — propose Tue 21 May 10:00am PT / Wed 22 May 01:00am SGT. Anita, if you can share availability, we'll lock it in.
